headline: Fuel prices jump by Tk20 a litre across Bangladesh, effective immediately
summary: The government has increased diesel to Tk135, petrol to Tk160, octane to Tk165, and kerosene to Tk155 per litre. A consumer rights advisor warns this will make survival extremely difficult for people.
details: The Bangladesh government has increased fuel prices by up to Tk20 per litre, effective from Sunday midnight. Under the new rates, diesel will be sold at Tk135, petrol at Tk160, octane at Tk165, and kerosene at Tk155 per litre.

This marks the latest in a series of hikes. Previously, on April 18, diesel increased by Tk15 to Tk115, petrol by Tk19 to Tk135, and octane by Tk20 to Tk140. Further increases of Tk5 for petrol, octane, and kerosene followed in June.

M Shamsul Alam, energy advisor for the Consumers Association of Bangladesh (CAB), expressed grave concerns. He stated that this hike, amidst inflation exceeding 8%, will make survival extremely difficult for people and further fuel price increases are anticipated.

The Ministry of Power, Energy, and Mineral Resources justified the increase by citing abnormal price rises in the international market due to ongoing conflicts in the Middle East. They noted that fuel prices in neighboring countries are significantly higher than in Bangladesh.

The Energy Division reported that the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) incurred a loss of Tk22,876 crore between March and August due to international price surges. Currently, BPC faces a loss of approximately Tk89 per litre on diesel, amounting to about Tk109 crore daily.

This daily loss on diesel alone translates to nearly Tk40,000 crore annually. The government aims to reduce BPC's annual losses by approximately Tk10,000 crore through this Tk20 per litre price adjustment.

Comparing regional prices, diesel costs Tk135 in Kolkata, Tk165 in Myanmar, Tk161 in Nepal, Tk179 in Sri Lanka, Tk151 in Thailand, and Tk185 in Pakistan. Maintaining lower prices in Bangladesh also poses a risk of fuel smuggling to neighboring countries.

The largest single fuel price hike in Bangladesh occurred in August 2022, when diesel increased by Tk34 per litre to Tk114, later reduced by Tk5. That increase significantly drove up commodity prices and transport fares nationwide.

headline: Case filed against MP Gazi Nazrul and two others over second wife’s death in Dhaka
summary: Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam and two others face charges of abetting the death of Mariam Khatun, whose body was found in a NAM Bhaban flat.
details: A case has been filed against Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam and two others, including his first wife, following the death of his second wife, Mariam Khatun. Mariam's hanging body was recovered from a flat at NAM Bhaban in Dhaka on Sunday night.

Mariam’s father, Masum Billah, filed the case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station late Sunday night. Gazi Nazrul’s first wife, Maksuda Begum, and Mariam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman are also named as accused.

Police confirmed that Gazi Nazrul was present at the flat when Mariam’s body was found. He and Maksuda were later taken to the police station for questioning. Authorities stated that due to his status as a lawmaker, specific legal procedures apply before any arrest can be made.
